Dependencies · Source: mqlite main · docs/dependencies.md — source v0.4.3 with unreleased changes. Latest supported release: v0.4.2. These docs track main; use the linked release for published artifacts.

Dependency policy & the go 1.21 floor

MQLite pins its go.mod floor at go 1.21 so the SDK stays drop-in embeddable in projects that haven't moved to a newer toolchain (MQLITE-1). That single decision freezes two dependencies — this note records why, what it costs, and how the freeze is enforced so it can't be lifted by accident.

Remote-only companion module

Applications that only call a broker can instead use the official MQLite Remote Client for Go. Its module path remains github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite-go; release target v0.1.2 has a Go 1.13 source floor and uses only the standard library, so it does not link the embedded engine, SQLite, libSQL/Turso, or CGO. The low floor is a compatibility promise, not a recommendation to run an end-of-life toolchain in production: build with a supported Go release whenever possible. Use this main module when an application needs embedded mode, transactional outbox, canonical observation decoding, or managed access-key administration.

What the floor freezes

dependency pinned next release why frozen
modernc.org/sqlite v1.36.1 v1.36.2 → go 1.23 the pure-Go SQLite engine; 1.36.1 is the last release that builds on go 1.21 — even the next patch bumped the floor to 1.23
golang.org/x/sys v0.30.0 v0.31.0 → go 1.23 transitive (file locking); v0.31.0+ all require go ≥ 1.23

There is no go-1.21-compatible upgrade for either — the very next version of each already requires go ≥ 1.23. So Dependabot bumps like sqlite → 1.52.0 or x/sys → 0.46.0 are not "upgrades we're behind on"; they are mutually exclusive with the go 1.21 floor and fail the go 1.21.x CI matrix by construction.

Remote libSQL driver

github.com/tursodatabase/libsql-client-go, the pure-Go Hrana client, is pinned even though upstream now marks the repository deprecated. This is a temporary compatibility choice, not an assertion that an unmaintained dependency is ideal. The upstream-recommended go-libsql uses CGO and currently publishes native libraries for only four Linux/macOS targets, while the newer tursogo module requires Go 1.24 and implements a local database plus remote synchronization rather than MQLite's current direct-primary Hrana path. The official tursogo-serverless module is a pure-Go database/sql driver that connects directly to Turso Cloud over HTTP, but its module also requires Go 1.24 and it has not passed MQLite's local/remote parity, live lifecycle, sustained-load or six-target release gates. None currently satisfies the complete Go 1.21, CGO-free, six-target and storage-semantics contract.

CI keeps that source-floor contract on supported macOS runners by externally linking the Go 1.21 test binaries. Go 1.21's internal Darwin linker does not emit the LC_UUID required by current macOS releases; the external Apple linker does. This exception applies only to the compatibility gate. Release binaries use the current supported Go toolchain and its normal linker selection.

MQLite contains the known HTTP logical-stream lifecycle defect behind a narrow single-lease adapter: a libsql:// driver connection is discarded when its database/sql lease ends, while Go's shared HTTP transport continues to reuse physical TCP/TLS connections. Migration to a maintained driver requires the full local/remote conformance suite, live Turso lifecycle and sustained-load runs, and all release-platform builds. Do not swap this dependency or remove the adapter based only on API similarity; there is no promised replacement or migration date.

The HTTP v2 transport and its protocol/result helpers are a small internal copy of that same pin (internal/libsqlcompat), with bounded asynchronous stream cleanup (MQLITE-164) and success-acknowledgement validation (MQLITE-191). Incomplete or mismatched replies cannot confirm success or authorize write replay. The original public SQL parser and WebSocket driver remain at the pin. Source/delta hashes and a module-version guard detect drift; there is no library-local replace or reliance on a caller's vendor directory. The copied MIT license and source notice ship with binary archives and container images. The existing ANTLR version is now listed directly because the copied helper imports it; dependency versions and the selected module graph are unchanged.

Security posture

Freezing requires checking upstream defects as well as running scanners. CI runs govulncheck on source and uses the GoReleaser release matrix to scan both actual binaries on all six OS/architecture pairs. Release hooks repeat those binary scans; Docker scans its actual output too. Artifacts retain symbols so the scanner can identify linked code instead of falling back to module-level matches. No advisory is excluded. A reachable vulnerability requires a fix or a deliberate change to the compatibility floor; the floor does not override security.

For example, GO-2026-5024 affects an x/sys/windows function that the current MQLite binaries do not call. Both Windows source analysis and symbol-preserving binary scans confirm that boundary. The binary gates must continue to pass if a later code/dependency change adds a call.

Go vulnerability scanning does not cover every native SQLite defect. SQLite's WAL-reset issue affects older SQLite versions when multiple connections concurrently write/checkpoint one WAL database. MQLite serializes local writes and checkpoints on one SQL connection. A second local connection serves observation reads with SQLite mode=ro and query_only, so it cannot write or checkpoint. Keep external backup connections read-only and never run another writer/checkpointer against the live file. The operations runbook preserves that restriction. Review native engine advisories before changing this connection model.

Container OS packages have a separate security boundary from Go dependencies. The runtime image upgrades installed APKs within the supported Alpine branch before adding certificates and time-zone data. A supported base tag can still contain older packages: Alpine 3.24.1 included OpenSSL 3.5.7, while its repository provides the 3.5.8 patch for CVE-2026-14456. The existing Docker CI job scans its actual image's OS packages independently of govulncheck, using a checksum-verified Trivy release and a fresh vulnerability database. HIGH/CRITICAL findings fail the job without advisory exclusions; its JSON report is retained as an artifact. Update the scanner version and checksum together after reviewing the official release. CI and release image builds bypass the runtime stage's cache so the APK upgrade runs even when the base tag is unchanged. The exact final release candidate image must also pass an OS scan before promotion. MQLite's static Go binary does not link these system OpenSSL libraries; that does not justify shipping avoidable vulnerable runtime packages.

How the freeze is enforced

  1. .github/dependabot.yml ignores modernc.org/sqlite >=1.36.2 and golang.org/x/sys >=0.31.0, so Dependabot stops opening PRs that can't merge.
  2. go 1.21.x CI matrix — a dependency (or a go.mod edit) that needs a newer toolchain fails to build there.
  3. TestGoModFloorStaysAt121 (sdk_test.go) asserts the floor is exactly go 1.21, failing with a clear message if it's bumped — so unfreezing the dependencies is always a conscious edit, never a side effect.

expr-lang/expr — the topic-filter dependency (MQLITE-17)

Subscription filters are an expr-lang/expr boolean predicate (see concepts.md § filters), a direct core dependency pinned at v1.17.8. It's a deliberate long-term choice: maintained by the expr-lang org (not a single author), zero transitive dependencies, MIT, and "memory-safe, side-effect-free, always-terminating" by construction — a sandboxed predicate evaluator. Its go.mod floor is only go 1.18, so it puts no pressure on the freeze above.

Security. The one relevant advisory, CVE-2025-29786 (parser memory exhaustion from an unbounded AST), is fixed in the v1.17.x line we pin. Defense in depth in engine/filter.go: a source-length cap + expr.MaxNodes, plus a fail-closed recover so a hostile or buggy filter can never crash the broker or silently match. (The CVSS-9.8 RCE search engines surface for "expr" is the JavaScript expr-eval library — a different project.) All filter use funnels through one wrapper, so an upstream change or evaluator swap touches one file; govulncheck (CI) covers expr at the pin.

When the freeze lifts

When the project intentionally raises the go floor (e.g. the embedding-compat requirement is dropped, or a security CVE forces it): bump go.mod, update TestGoModFloorStaysAt121 and this table, remove the Dependabot ignore rules, and let the held bumps (modernc.org/sqlite, golang.org/x/sys) flow in together.
